subject: English
q: The house ______ we bought last year needs repairs.
explanation: ‘Which’ (or ‘that’) refers to things; ‘who’ and ‘whom’ refer to people.

subject: English
q: This is the best film ______ I have ever seen.
explanation: After a superlative, ‘that’ is the preferred relative pronoun.

subject: English
q: All ______ glitters is not gold.
explanation: After ‘all’, ‘that’ is the preferred relative pronoun.

subject: English
q: The shepherd and his dog ______ were crossing the stream were swept away.
explanation: When the antecedent includes both a person and an animal, ‘that’ is used.

subject: English
q: Give the prize to ______ deserves it most.
explanation: The pronoun is the subject of ‘deserves’, so ‘whoever’ is correct even after ‘to’.

subject: English
q: I did exactly ______ I was told.
explanation: ‘What’ means ‘the thing(s) that’ and has no antecedent.

subject: English
q: Such students ______ work hard will be rewarded.
explanation: After ‘such’, the relative pronoun is ‘as’.

subject: English
q: This is the village ______ my grandfather was born.
explanation: A relative clause about a place, without a preposition, is introduced by ‘where’.

subject: English
q: The boy hurt ______ while playing football.
explanation: When the object is the same as the subject, a reflexive pronoun is used; ‘hisself’ is non-standard.

subject: English
q: The players blamed ______ for the defeat.
explanation: A plural subject takes the reflexive ‘themselves’.

subject: English
q: The manager ______ signed the letter of apology.
explanation: An emphatic pronoun stresses the subject; the standard form is ‘himself’.

subject: English
q: We really enjoyed ______ at the wedding.
explanation: ‘Enjoy’ in this sense needs a reflexive object, and a plural subject takes ‘ourselves’.

subject: English
q: Children, please behave ______ while the guests are here.
explanation: When addressing more than one person, the reflexive is ‘yourselves’.

subject: English
q: When he heard the verdict, he was beside ______ with rage.
explanation: The idiom is ‘beside oneself’, so the reflexive form is required.

subject: English
q: Since his children moved abroad, the old man lives by ______.
explanation: ‘By oneself’ means ‘alone’ and requires the reflexive pronoun.

subject: English
q: Each of the students must bring ______ own lunch.
explanation: ‘Each’ is singular, so the possessive must be singular and refer to people.

subject: English
q: Everyone in the unit is expected to do ______ duty.
explanation: ‘Everyone’ is singular and refers to people, so a singular personal possessive is used.

subject: English
q: Neither of the girls has finished ______ homework.
explanation: ‘Neither’ is singular, so it takes the singular pronoun ‘her’ for girls.

subject: English
q: One should always respect ______ elders.
explanation: When the subject is ‘one’, the matching possessive is ‘one’s’.

subject: English
q: The committee has submitted ______ report to the minister.
explanation: A collective noun acting as a single body takes a singular verb (‘has’) and the singular pronoun ‘its’.

subject: English
q: The jury were divided in ______ opinions.
explanation: When a collective noun refers to members acting individually, it takes a plural verb and ‘their’.

subject: English
q: Either the manager or his assistants will present ______ findings.
explanation: With ‘either … or’, the pronoun agrees with the nearer antecedent (assistants), so ‘their’ is used.

subject: English
q: Either Ahmed or Bilal will lend you ______ car.
explanation: Two singular antecedents joined by ‘either … or’ take a singular pronoun.

subject: English
q: Ali and Sara have finished ______ work.
explanation: Two antecedents joined by ‘and’ take a plural pronoun.

subject: English
q: Pakistan must protect ______ interests in the region.
explanation: A country treated as a political unit takes the pronoun ‘its’; ‘it’s’ means ‘it is’.

subject: English
q: I do not mind ______ coming late once in a while.
explanation: In formal English a possessive is used before a gerund (your coming).

subject: English
q: That red umbrella is ______.
explanation: The possessive pronoun standing alone is ‘mine’; it never takes an apostrophe.

subject: English
q: This house is not rented; it is ______.
explanation: Possessive pronouns such as ‘ours’ and ‘yours’ have no apostrophe.

subject: English
q: He is an old friend of ______.
explanation: The double possessive uses ‘of’ plus a possessive pronoun: a friend of mine.

subject: English
q: The dog wagged ______ tail when its owner came home.
explanation: ‘Its’ is the possessive form; ‘it’s’ means ‘it is’ or ‘it has’.

subject: English
q: Our car is old, but ______ is brand new.
explanation: A possessive pronoun that stands alone is ‘theirs’, with no apostrophe.

subject: English
q: The climate of Murree is cooler than ______ of Lahore.
explanation: A singular noun (climate) is replaced by ‘that’ to avoid repetition in a comparison.

subject: English
q: Property prices in Karachi are lower than ______ in Islamabad.
explanation: A plural noun (prices) is replaced by ‘those’ in a comparison.

subject: English
q: ______ who work hard usually succeed.
explanation: ‘Those who’ means ‘the people who’; ‘them’ cannot be followed by a relative clause in this way.

subject: English
q: ______ books on the top shelf belong to the library.
explanation: ‘Them’ is an object pronoun and cannot be used as a determiner before a noun; ‘those’ is correct with a plural noun.

subject: English
q: ______ of the two roads will take you to the city.
explanation: ‘Either’ refers to one of two; ‘any’ is used for more than two.

subject: English
q: You may borrow ______ of these five books.
explanation: For a choice among more than two, ‘any’ is used; ‘either’ is for two.

subject: English
q: ______ of these two pens is yours?
explanation: ‘Which’ is used when asking about a choice from a limited set.

subject: English
q: I invited five friends, but ______ of them turned up.
explanation: ‘None’ is used with ‘of’ plus a plural noun or pronoun; ‘no one’ and ‘nobody’ are not followed by ‘of’.

subject: English
q: The two brothers have not spoken to ______ since their father’s death.
explanation: A reciprocal relationship between people is expressed by ‘each other’; ‘themselves’ is reflexive.

subject: English
q: In the sentence ‘The family sat round the fire’, the word ‘round’ is:
explanation: ‘Round’ here links the noun ‘fire’ to the verb and shows position, so it is a preposition.

subject: English
q: In the sentence ‘He came back after ten years’, the word ‘back’ is:
explanation: ‘Back’ modifies the verb ‘came’, telling where, so it is an adverb.

subject: English
q: In the sentence ‘Please use the back door’, the word ‘back’ is:
explanation: ‘Back’ qualifies the noun ‘door’, so it is an adjective.

subject: English
q: In the sentence ‘I am not feeling well today’, the word ‘well’ is:
explanation: After a linking verb, ‘well’ meaning ‘in good health’ describes the subject, so it is an adjective.

subject: English
q: In the sentence ‘He left for Dubai in 2015 and I have not seen him since’, the word ‘since’ is:
explanation: Standing alone without an object or clause, ‘since’ means ‘from then until now’ and is an adverb.

subject: English
q: In the sentence ‘The shop has been closed since Monday’, the word ‘since’ is:
explanation: ‘Since’ followed by a noun (Monday) is a preposition.

subject: English
q: In the sentence ‘Since you insist, I will go with you’, the word ‘since’ is:
explanation: ‘Since’ introduces a clause (you insist) giving a reason, so it is a conjunction.

subject: English
q: In the sentence ‘I have seen this film before’, the word ‘before’ is:
explanation: ‘Before’ used without an object means ‘earlier’ and is an adverb.

subject: English
q: In the sentence ‘He is but a child’, the word ‘but’ is:
explanation: Here ‘but’ means ‘only’ and modifies the phrase ‘a child’, so it is an adverb.

subject: English
q: In the sentence ‘Everyone but Ahmed was present’, the word ‘but’ is:
explanation: ‘But’ meaning ‘except’ and followed by a noun is a preposition.

subject: English
q: In the sentence ‘That book on the table is mine’, the word ‘that’ is:
explanation: ‘That’ placed before a noun (book) points it out, so it is a demonstrative adjective.

subject: English
q: In the sentence ‘I know that he is honest’, the word ‘that’ is:
explanation: ‘That’ introduces the noun clause ‘he is honest’, so it is a conjunction.

subject: English
q: In the sentence ‘He looks like his father’, the word ‘like’ is:
explanation: ‘Like’ meaning ‘similar to’ and followed by a noun phrase is a preposition.

subject: English
q: In the sentence ‘Winter is drawing near’, the word ‘near’ is:
explanation: ‘Near’ modifies the verb ‘drawing’ and has no object, so it is an adverb.

subject: English
q: In the sentence ‘He lives near the mosque’, the word ‘near’ is:
explanation: ‘Near’ followed by a noun (the mosque) is a preposition.

subject: English
q: In the sentence ‘She is old enough to vote’, the word ‘enough’ is:
explanation: ‘Enough’ modifies the adjective ‘old’, so it is an adverb.

subject: English
q: In the sentence ‘I do not like crowded places much’, the word ‘much’ is:
explanation: ‘Much’ modifies the verb ‘like’, so it is an adverb.

subject: English
q: In the sentence ‘All is well that ends well’, the word ‘all’ is:
explanation: ‘All’ stands alone as the subject in place of a noun, so it is a pronoun.

subject: English
q: In the sentence ‘The late president was buried in his native village’, the word ‘late’ is:
explanation: ‘Late’ (meaning ‘deceased’) qualifies the noun ‘president’, so it is an adjective.

subject: English
q: In the sentence ‘The train arrived late’, the word ‘late’ is:
explanation: ‘Late’ modifies the verb ‘arrived’, so it is an adverb.

subject: English
q: In the sentence ‘She reads a daily newspaper’, the word ‘daily’ is:
explanation: ‘Daily’ qualifies the noun ‘newspaper’, so it is an adjective.

subject: English
q: In the sentence ‘She exercises daily’, the word ‘daily’ is:
explanation: ‘Daily’ modifies the verb ‘exercises’, telling how often, so it is an adverb.

subject: English
q: In the sentence ‘The water in the lake was still’, the word ‘still’ is:
explanation: After the linking verb ‘was’, ‘still’ (motionless) describes the noun ‘water’, so it is an adjective.

subject: English
q: In the sentence ‘He is still working on the report’, the word ‘still’ is:
explanation: ‘Still’ (continuing) modifies the verb ‘is working’, so it is an adverb.

subject: English
q: In the sentence ‘I have not read the novel, and my sister has not either’, the word ‘either’ is:
explanation: At the end of a negative clause, ‘either’ means ‘also’ and is an adverb.

subject: English
q: In the sentence ‘You can take either road to the village’, the word ‘either’ is:
explanation: ‘Either’ placed before a noun (road) qualifies it, so it is an adjective.

subject: English
q: In the sentence ‘The old wall fell down’, the word ‘down’ is:
explanation: ‘Down’ has no object and modifies the verb ‘fell’, so it is an adverb.

subject: English
q: In the sentence ‘The children ran down the hill’, the word ‘down’ is:
explanation: ‘Down’ followed by a noun phrase (the hill) is a preposition.

subject: English
q: In the sentence ‘He is poor, yet he is honest’, the word ‘yet’ is:
explanation: ‘Yet’ joins two clauses and shows contrast, so it is a conjunction.

subject: English
q: In the sentence ‘He was absent, for he was ill’, the word ‘for’ is:
explanation: ‘For’ joining two clauses to give a reason is a coordinating conjunction.

subject: English
q: In the sentence ‘He worked as a clerk for many years’, the word ‘as’ is:
explanation: ‘As’ followed by a noun phrase and meaning ‘in the role of’ is a preposition.

subject: English
q: In the sentence ‘There were about fifty people at the meeting’, the word ‘about’ is:
explanation: ‘About’ meaning ‘approximately’ modifies the number ‘fifty’, so it is an adverb.

subject: English
q: In the sentence ‘The procession moved past the Governor’s House’, the word ‘past’ is:
explanation: ‘Past’ followed by a noun phrase is a preposition.

subject: English
q: In the sentence ‘A nation that forgets its past cannot shape its future’, the word ‘past’ is:
explanation: ‘Past’ is the object of ‘forgets’ and is preceded by ‘its’, so it is a noun.

subject: English
q: In the sentence ‘Alas! The old man has passed away’, the word ‘alas’ is:
explanation: ‘Alas’ expresses sudden grief and has no grammatical link with the rest of the sentence, so it is an interjection.

subject: English
q: In the sentence ‘It started raining, so the children played inside’, the word ‘inside’ is:
explanation: ‘Inside’ has no object and modifies the verb ‘played’, so it is an adverb.

subject: English
q: In the sentence ‘He is quick to take offence’, the word ‘quick’ is:
explanation: After the linking verb ‘is’, ‘quick’ describes the subject, so it is an adjective.

subject: English
q: In the sentence ‘The soldiers marched forward’, the word ‘forward’ is:
explanation: ‘Forward’ modifies the verb ‘marched’ and shows direction, so it is an adverb.

subject: English
q: In the sentence ‘It was a hard decision to make’, the word ‘hard’ is:
explanation: ‘Hard’ qualifies the noun ‘decision’, so it is an adjective.

subject: English
q: In which sentence is ‘round’ used as an adverb?
o: The boxer lost the first round.
The children gathered round to hear the story.
explanation: In ‘gathered round’ the word has no object and modifies the verb; elsewhere it is an adjective, a preposition and a noun.
